findings.summary: Independent affected and full rosters would recreate gate divergence.
findings.disposition: D1 uses one resolver for dynamic full discovery and affected narrowing, with an acknowledged roster digest.

findings.summary: Retained gate logs require an explicit privacy, concurrency, and retention contract.
findings.disposition: D1 specifies a private Git-common-dir run store, allowlisted metadata, independent redaction, atomic writes, and retention.

findings.summary: A manual documentation ownership map would become a second authority.
findings.disposition: D4 makes current state output-only and provenance-bound to existing gate, parity, and capability authorities.

findings.summary: Family defaults could silently acknowledge a newly discovered host asset.
findings.disposition: D3 requires a human-acknowledged canonical inventory digest before defaults expand.

findings.summary: Affected scope must include committed, staged, unstaged, untracked, rename, delete, and submodule state.
findings.disposition: D2 unions all Git worktree sources and falls back to full for every unclassifiable or assurance-bearing path.

findings.summary: Host parity must prove installed activation rather than inventory labels.
findings.disposition: D3 requires supported rows to identify binding and liveness, then verifies both installed host compositions in scratch repositories.

findings.summary: A review findings ledger without a gate consumer would be write-only.
findings.disposition: D5 adds a dynamically discovered full-gate validator with unresolved-blocker, false-closure, duplicate-ID, and scope-SHA plants.
